name: evaluate-two-quad-patches-a-patch-id-apart-in-one-tessellated-draw
rationale:
The first authored case on a quad-domain patch, and the first that gives a tessellated draw more than one patch. 224 of the 233 post-tessellation corpus sources are quad patches of 16 control points, against 9 triangles; the triangle domain is covered by the case on eMHMCLaTPglgf6yx and nothing had reached this one. This host is also representative in the other way that matters: 222 of the 224 declare no patch_control_point_input at all and read their control points from ordinary device buffers indexed by air.patch_id, so the patch identity itself is on the observation path.

The draw is two patches with edge factors 1,1,1,1 and inside factors 1,1, so the tessellator emits each patch as its four corners. At u and v in {0,1} the cubic Bernstein weights are exactly (1,0,0,0) or (0,0,0,1) and the accumulation starts from a zeroed row, so each generated vertex carries EXACTLY the corner control point, with no rounding anywhere in the Bezier evaluation.

Patch 0's corners are the screen rectangle x in [-1,0], y in [-1,1]; patch 1's are x in [0,1], y in [-1,1]. On the 4x4 target the pixel centres sit at x = -0.75, -0.25, +0.25, +0.75, so patch 0 owns the left two columns and patch 1 the right two, and no pixel centre lies on the shared edge at x = 0. If air.patch_id did not reach the control-point buffer, both patches would read set 0 and the right half would keep its 0xab initial bytes instead.

The 16 control points of each patch are the bilinear grid over its four corners, so P(u,v) is an affine function of (u,v) and therefore of screen position, with w = 1 everywhere. That makes the observed varying independent of which diagonal splits the tessellated quad into two triangles, which is the one thing about the quad domain a corner-only case could otherwise not control. The z of the control points is what carries the information: it is 0.0625 + 0.375u + 0.1875v on patch 0 and 0.5 - 0.375u + 0.1875v on patch 1, opposite slopes in u, and every value is a multiple of 1/64 inside the depth range.

The observation is varying 0, position = modelViewTransform * float4(P, 1), and the whole path to it is exact: modelViewTransform is diag(2,4,8) with translation (0.5, 0.25, 0.125), and projectionTransform is its exact inverse diag(0.5, 0.25, 0.125) with translation (-0.25, -0.0625, -0.015625), so the clip position is P itself while the varying is (2Px + 0.5, 4Py + 0.25, 8Pz + 0.125) -- a value the rasterizer cannot hand back for free. Every constant is a power of two, so no step of either matrix product rounds. patchParamBuffer is zero, which makes the refinement level 0 and the derivative scale exactly 3; that scale only reaches varying 1, the normal, which this case does not observe, so no air.fast_rsqrt result is on the expectation path.

All 16 pixels were derived before the run and Metal writes exactly them: lane 0 is 2x + 0.5 = -1, 0, 1, 2 across each row, lane 1 is 4y + 0.25 = 3.25, 1.25, -0.75, -2.75 down each column, and lane 2 is 8Pz + 0.125, which is 2.6875, 4.1875, 4.6875, 3.1875 on the top row -- rising across patch 0 and falling across patch 1, which is the sign of the patch's own u slope. MoltenVK matches exactly.

What this case does NOT pin: exchanging the two TessCoord components maps a quad patch onto the same four corners in the reverse ring order, so no quantity that is a function of the corner position can see it. Only the surface normal can, through the sign of cross(dP/du, dP/dv), and that value leaves the shader through air.fast_rsqrt, which is not derivable by hand. The u/v orientation of the quad domain therefore remains unpinned here.

execution_safety is authored_bounded: the two nested loops that evaluate the tensor-product basis are counted 0..4 against a literal 4, with no input on either bound, and the patch-parameter shift is masked to 5 bits before use.

name: an-effect-free-mesh-function-draws-nothing-without-rasterization
rationale: mesh_object_grid_mesh sets its primitive count to 0 from thread 0 and sets no vertex or primitive, and binds and writes no memory: it has no effect a stage observes. Drawn without rasterization under a grid of 2 threadgroups of 2 threads, with no fragment function, the draw must complete and its exact observable output is the empty byte sequence.

name: swap-two-device-structs-through-a-local-including-the-padding
rationale: A device struct swapped through a stack local is TWO memcpys the emitter has to lower in opposite directions, and neither had an authored case. Corner is float2 + float: twelve bytes of members in a sixteen-byte object, and Metal's own front end lowers all three assignments to llvm.memcpy of 16 bytes, so the four padding bytes travel with the value. Raw device buffer to typed local goes through emit_raw_to_typed_struct_memcpy / emit_raw_to_typed_aggregate_fields / emit_raw_word_as_typed_memcpy_field / emit_raw_word_as_typed_scalar (41 corpus sources each); typed local back to raw device buffer goes through emit_typed_to_raw_memcpy / collect_typed_memcpy_words / typed_memcpy_word (21 each). The return leg is the interesting one: reading the local as a typed value yields only THREE words -- the two float2 lanes and the float -- for a sixteen-byte copy, so the padding word cannot come from the typed value at all. typed_memcpy_words_with_raw_padding (16 sources) recovers it from the shadow the forward leg recorded, which is the only reason a byte-faithful swap is possible. The AIR is hand-written because the smallest corpus host that reaches all six is 222 lines of loop-carried corner sorting over five buffers, and it is byte-identical in shape to what xcrun emits for the .metal beside this file. The two padding words are distinct (0x11223344 and 0x55667788) so that a lowering which drops the padding, or writes zero there, or leaves the destination's own padding in place, answers differently from one that swaps all sixteen bytes. The six float members are exact small binary32 integers.

name: sample-the-second-probe-of-a-cube-array-whose-slices-disagree
rationale: The fragment samples a texturecube_array<half> at an explicit level zero using its normal varying as the direction and its flat uint varying as the array slice, and returns the half4 unchanged. All six faces of a slice carry one value and the two slices carry different values, so the face the direction selects cannot matter while the slice index still decides the whole result: reading slice zero instead of slice one gives a visibly different pixel. This is the corpus's first cube array, so it is the first case to exercise the Metal TypeCubeArray and Vulkan CUBE_ARRAY view paths and the layer-major packing of six faces per slice.

name: divide-by-a-runtime-and-a-constant-denominator
rationale: Integer division and remainder in the two shapes the denominator guard distinguishes. Rows 0-7 divide by a RUNTIME denominator at every width and lane count the pass handles -- uint, int, uint2, ulong scalar div and rem -- so the emitted module keeps seven live `denom == 0 ? 1 : denom` guards; the last row reads through a runtime byte offset, which the translator turns into a word index with its OWN `/ 4`, and that constant denominator takes no guard at all. Every divisor is non-zero on every lane, so the guarded and unguarded paths must agree with Metal identically and the case does not depend on divide-by-zero, which is undefined in MSL. The dividends are 5, -5, 0, INT_MIN, INT_MAX, -1, 1 and 0x7F000000 against divisors 3, 3, 7, 7, 3, INT_MAX, 0xFFFFFFFF and 4: signed rows cross zero in both operands (so a wrong truncation direction shows as a sign flip), no lane is INT_MIN / -1, and lane 2's dividend of 0 pins the zero-numerator answer. The v2uint row's second lane divides `ua >> 3` by `ub | 1`, a different value per lane, so a splatted vector guard cannot pass. The raw row indexes RAW by `ua & 7`, which hits six distinct words. The output buffer is 320 bytes but only 288 are written, so the trailing eight words must still hold their 0xCD fill.

name: reduce-eight-points-to-a-bounding-box-through-threadgroup-float-bit-atomics
rationale:
The float-as-signed-int threadgroup atomic min/max idiom, which the corpus reaches through exactly one host -- an 841-line BVH builder -- so no authored case reached `native/wg_atomic.rs` at all. Measured with per-function coverage against every cased source: this fixture reaches 25 functions no cased source reaches, being all 11 of `native/wg_atomic.rs` (`remodel_one`, `clone_f2i`, `rewrite_bodies`, `find_ptr`, `is_atomic` and their closures), 11 of the 14 in `passes/workgroup/atomic_loop.rs` (`apply_unroll_plan`, `counted_trip_count`, `remap_operand`, `splice_unrolled_preheader`, `unique_unconditional_preheader`), and `emitter::ops::atomics::bitcast_pointer_to_atomic_i32`, `pointers::raw_select::emit_raw_pointer_select_index` and `tir::operands::extract_aggregate_member`. Only `atomic_loop::const_bool`, the trip-2 bool-toggle variant of the trip count, is left uncovered.

Two lowerings meet on this shape. Logical SPIR-V forbids an `OpBitcast` of a pointer, so the emitter cannot name the int at a threadgroup float's address; `wg_atomic` instead RETYPES the Workgroup variable's float leaves to the int32 the atomics use -- the same tree shape at the same byte offsets, so every access-chain index is unchanged -- and rewrites the plain float loads and stores of that same variable into value bitcasts. The threadgroup object is `struct Box { float lo[3]; float hi[3]; }` precisely so the clone has to walk a nested struct-of-arrays rather than a scalar. Separately, the axis loop is one block, counted, barrier-free and holds two Workgroup atomics, so `unroll_small_workgroup_atomic_loops` flattens its three iterations before the structurizer sees it; `#pragma clang loop unroll(disable)` is what stops the Metal frontend from unrolling it first and leaving nothing to measure.

The comparison is exact even though eight threads race, because atomic min and max are commutative and associative: the final value of each of the six accumulators does not depend on the interleaving. Every input is a small integer-valued float, exactly representable in binary32, and the compare runs on the order-preserving encoding -- the bit pattern for a non-negative float, and the bit pattern with its low 31 bits flipped for a negative one, which reverses the descending order of negative bit patterns into the ascending order a signed compare wants. Thread t contributes (t - 4, 2t - 9, 10 - t) for t in 0..7, so axes 0 and 1 carry negatives and fail visibly if the flip is dropped or if the compare is unsigned (an unsigned min over axis 0 answers 0 rather than -4, because every negative encoding has its high bit set), while axis 2 is all-positive and exercises the unflipped branch. The six answers -- lo (-4, -9, 3) and hi (3, 5, 10) -- are pairwise distinguishable per axis and between lo and hi, so a transposed axis index or a swapped min/max is visible rather than silent. Metal answered exactly those six floats, derived in advance, and MoltenVK Matches.

Each accumulator starts from a sentinel the kernel never writes: `lo` from FLT_MAX, whose bit pattern 0x7f7fffff is at least the encoding of every finite float, and `hi` from -0.0f, whose bit pattern 0x80000000 is the smallest signed int. A dropped initial read leaves FLT_MAX or a NaN in the output, and the output buffer is pre-filled with -1.0, which no arm can produce.

`authored_bounded`: all three loops are `for (uint a = 0; a < 3; ++a)` over a literal bound of 3 with no early exit and no data-dependent condition, so each runs exactly three iterations. The dispatch is one threadgroup of eight threads, which is the literal length of the input the kernel indexes.

name: broadcast-a-quad-and-reduce-halves-two-ways
rationale: Six uncovered subgroup families in one 32-lane simdgroup -- air.quad_is_first (6 corpus sources), air.quad_shuffle_xor.v4f16 (5), air.quad_broadcast.v4f32 (5), air.simd_sum.v4f16 (4), air.quad_sum.v4f16 (4) and air.quad_shuffle_down.u.v4i32 (4). The half lanes carry small integers so that both reductions are association-proof: half is exact on integers up to 2048 and the largest column totals 1552, so every accumulation order gives the same bits, while the per-lane and per-component values still differ enough that a reduction over the wrong lane set cannot match. The two reductions separate the lane models -- quad_sum clusters to four lanes and simd_sum to all thirty-two, so the eight quads report eight different quad sums (16q+10 and 16q+138) against one common simd sum. quad_shuffle_xor with mask 1 and quad_broadcast with index 2 stay inside the quad for every lane; quad_shuffle_down with delta 1 leaves the last lane of each quad undefined, and those slots are overwritten with a constant on a branch over tid rather than asserted on. All 576 words were derived by hand before the GPU was asked.

name: clamp-to-zero-texels-of-r16float-r16uint-rgba16sint
rationale: clamp_to_zero addressing per bound pixel format (the Metal-oracle check of ClampToZero and the border and alpha observations; The product maps it to Vulkan's CLAMP_TO_BORDER with a transparent-black border and leaves open whether that border gives alpha 1 on a format without alpha, which Metal documents as (0, 0, 0, 1) there and (0, 0, 0, 0) with alpha; The product keeps such a sampler off the exact pixel fetch for that reason). This case binds r16_float to the float texture 0, r16_uint to the uint texture 1, and rgba16_sint to the int texture 2, each 4x4 with every texel equal: the float texture's channels hold 1.0 (0xFF for unorm), the uint texture's (1, 2, 3, 4) and the int texture's (-1, 2, -3, 4), truncated to the format's channels. Lane t reads a normalized coordinate from buffer 0 and writes five uint4s of raw bits to buffer 1: the float texture through the constexpr nearest clamp_to_zero sampler (out[5t]), the constexpr linear clamp_to_zero sampler (out[5t+1]), and the runtime sampler at [[sampler(0)]], which the case sets to nearest clamp_to_zero, normalized, not mipmapped (out[5t+2]); then the uint (out[5t+3]) and int (out[5t+4]) textures through the constexpr nearest sampler, all at explicit level 0. The coordinates are (0.125, 0.125), (0.875, 0.625), (-0.125, 0.375), (1.125, 0.375), (0.375, -0.125), (0.375, 1.125), (-0.125, -0.125), (1.5, 1.5), (0, 0.375), (1, 0.375), (0.375, 0), (0.375, 1), (0, 0), (-0.0625, 0.375), (1.0625, 0.625), (0.625, 0.625): texel centres inside, points outside each side and corner, and points on each edge and a quarter texel outside, so nearest lanes outside read the zero texel itself (and a nearest sample at u = 1.0 selects texel 4, outside) while linear lanes on an edge blend the in-range texel with the zero texel at weights 1/2 (edges), 1/4 and 3/4 (the corner and the quarter-texel lanes), which shows the zero texel's alpha after filtering. All in-range values and weights are dyadic, so every expected value is exact. The runtime column should equal the constexpr nearest column. The output is pre-filled with 0xAB so an unwritten word is visible; each lane writes only its own five uint4s; the AIR has no loop.

name: linked-single-nearest-write
rationale: One invocation covers a unit source and destination. Unit dimensions and scale with zero translation select coordinate zero, the function constant selects unit-batch nearest-floor resampling, the reference-size constant exposes one device-buffer slot, and the linked prefix/postfix pair writes exact one to element zero.

name: quad-votes-over-every-active-subset-of-a-quad
rationale: Settles the Metal reading of divergent quad votes. One threadgroup of 64 threads; compute quads are four consecutive threads. Lane t & 3 of quad q = t >> 2 enters the branch exactly when bit (t & 3) of q is set, so the sixteen quads cover every subset of a quad once: the empty one (quad 0 writes only the 0xFF000000 marker), single lanes, and subsets whose first lane is inactive (quads 2, 4, 6, 8, 10, 12, 14). An active lane packs quad_is_first (bit 0), quad_active_threads_mask (bits 1-4), quad_all(t even) (bit 5), quad_any(t % 5 == 0) (bit 6), quad_all(t != 9) (bit 7) and quad_any(t == 9) (bit 8). Metal's backend keeps this arm (measured on the M3 Max, macOS 27.0.1; air::canon::speculate leaves it too), so only active lanes vote: the mask equals q, is_first is set on the lowest active lane, and an inactive lane's predicate never enters an all/any (quad 2's only active lane is thread 9, so there quad_all(t != 9) is false and quad_any(t == 9) true; quad 1's only active lane is thread 4, so quad_all(t even) is true there although its inactive lane 5 is odd). The whole word differs from the 0xAB poison on every thread. The AIR has no loop.

name: lim8-int2-dequantize-two-codes-per-thread-with-zero-points
rationale: Reaching variant of the zero-limit case of this entry, whose lim = 0 stops every thread before its first load. Eight threads (lim = 8, one threadgroup) each dequantize two adjacent 2-bit codes (loadLen 2 from quantizedFC bits 27 to 32): dim0Div (8, magic 0, shift 3) maps thread t to element 2t of one 16-element row, the other dimensions are 1. The table holds four entries (MPSNDArrayRefSize sums to 4): the packed codes at entry 0 (matrixIndex), the destination at entry 1, four float scales at entry 2 (scaleIndex, isScaleFloat) and four packed 2-bit unsigned zero points at entry 3 (zeropointIndex, isZeroPoint); no minimum value. Dimension 0 takes group attribute 7, so element c reads group c >> log2GroupSize = c >> 2 through the generic (splat) path; dimensions 1 to 3 take attribute 1. Element c is scale[c >> 2] * (q[c] - zp[c >> 2]) with scales 0.5, 2, 1, 4 and nonlinear codes q[c] = ((c^2 + 3c + 1) + floor(c/3)) mod 4, so a wrong element, group or nibble changes the answer. Codes and zero points convert exactly through half, every difference is a small integer and every scale a power of two, so each result is exact. The identity destination lanes (destIndexFC 0, 1, 2, 3) give the linked writer, which stores table entry 1 at the column coordinate, columns 2t and 2t + 1: each of the 16 observed words is written once. No loop depends on the data: the group-index loop and the lane loops have constant trip counts and lim bounds the threads.

name: linked-zero-limit-i4-dequantize
no_effect: The authored parameters give the work an empty extent, so the entry returns before any write reaches the selected output.
rationale: The exact 240-byte parameter record sets lim to zero. The sole invocation has thread index zero, so the top-level unsigned lim comparison is false and every reachable dequantization and write loop is bypassed. The sole poisoned linked destination remains byte-exact while both retained postfix dependencies are authored explicitly for linkage. Replaced: the linked destination callback writes table entry 1, so the case binds a two-entry table (MPSNDArrayRefSize 1 source, 1 destination) whose destination element carries the source element's fill.

The exact linked callback returns float4 zero without dereferencing resources; the poisoned global bin makes the local-atomic aggregation observable byte-exactly.

name: widen-three-hdr-planes-after-a-sixteen-bit-shift
rationale:
A 3-plane HDR10 fragment shader reading Y, U and V as separate ushort textures and packing them into one uint render target. It covers air.convert.u.v3i32.u.v3i16, which no case reached before; 22 corpus sources carry it.
The widen is only interesting because of what precedes it. The three plane samples are assembled into a <3 x i16> and shifted left by two IN SIXTEEN BITS, so bits 14 and 15 are lost, and only then does air.convert.u.v3i32.u.v3i16 zero-extend to i32. 33 of the 48 plane values here are at least 16384, so they do lose bits: a widen performed before the shift, or one that sign-extended rather than zero-extended, gives a different answer for two thirds of the samples.
Every value is an exact integer and the whole shader is integer arithmetic after the sample, so there is nothing to associate and nothing to round. The three planes carry three different arithmetic progressions mod 65536, so a plane read in place of another shows; all 16 output pixels are distinct.
The sampler is nearest with normalized coordinates and the textures are exactly the render target's size, so the harness's fragment varying ((px+0.5)/W, 1-(py+0.5)/H) lands on texel centres and every read is unambiguous -- the answer does not depend on the filter. The vertical flip that varying implies is part of the derivation rather than something to design around.
Both arms of the chroma select are exercised: position.x is px+0.5, ushort() truncates it to px, and the low bit picks U on even columns and V on odd ones. Every even column differs from its odd neighbour, so an inverted or dropped select is visible.
The uniforms buffer is air.arg_unused and the texcoord varying is too; both are still declared, because reflection reports the interface the shader declares rather than the one it reads.

name: irreducible-two-entry-cycle-through-the-state-machine-construction
rationale:
No authored case reaches the state-machine CFG construction in `src/native/relooper.rs`: 60 of its 73 corpus-reached functions had zero case coverage, the second-largest such gap after `opaque_image_select.rs`. The reason is structural -- cases are always picked as the SMALLEST OK host for a symbol, so they are single-function modules with reducible control flow, and the relooper only runs on what the nesting structurizer declines. 80 corpus sources do reach a successful relooper rewrite, but the smallest is 22 KB of MLX, far too large to derive an expected output for by hand.

So this is an owned fixture instead. `%a` and `%b` form a cycle that `%entry` enters at BOTH of them. No header dominates the cycle, so it is irreducible, SPIR-V structured control flow cannot spell it, `reloop_nest` declines it (`irreducible control flow`, 7 blocks) and the state machine takes it -- which is the only way to reach the spill/restore and phi-edge stores this file is here to check. The Metal front end cannot be made to emit that shape from any source text, so the `.ll` is hand-written and the sibling `.metal` -- which is what Metal actually runs -- is the same automaton with one entry: state `(i, acc, in_b)`, step `acc = in_b ? acc+5 : acc*3`, `i += 1`, exit when `i >= n`, else flip `in_b`. The two spellings differ ONLY in control-flow shape; every arithmetic operation, constant and initial value is identical, and `acc` is seeded 2 when the cycle is entered at `%b` and 1 when it is entered at `%a` exactly as the ternary seeds it.

`input[tid] = tid` over a 32-thread grid, so n runs 0..31: both entry parities, both exit arms, trip counts from 1 (n=0 still executes one step, and answers 3) to 31, and an `acc` that interleaves the two arms differently for every thread. A relooper that dropped a phi edge, restored a spill from the wrong arm, or picked the wrong initial dispatch state would answer the OTHER parity's sequence and every thread would move. The comparison is exact because both arms are integer.
